name: Google Workspace Reports API (further applications)
description: Google Workspace Reports API activity for the 13 applications the gws pack does not bind (saml, token, context_aware_access, access_transparency, mobile, chrome, groups_enterprise, rules, calendar, chat, data_studio, gcp, gemini_in_workspace_apps): who did what, in which application, from where. Only gws:reports:data_studio has a captured sample; the rest carry only the Reports API envelope every application shares.
source: Google Workspace Admin SDK Reports API, activities resource and the per-application event appendices; the Splunk Add-on for Google Workspace's own preprocessing and props stanzas, read from the installed add-on and cross-checked one sourcetype at a time. Only gws:reports:data_studio carries a captured sample; the other twelve applications are documented from the reference alone.

feed.label: Google Workspace Reports API (further applications)
feed.description: Thirteen further Reports API applications beyond the gws pack's login, admin and drive: one record per event, actor and id nested, event.parameters an array.

event_time.label: Event time
event_time.description: When the activity happened, id.time on the Activity item: UTC, ISO 8601 with milliseconds. The TA's props.conf reads _time from it; ingestion lags behind it.

actor_email.label: Actor email
actor_email.description: The email of the user or admin the activity item is about (actor.email).

actor_profile_id.label: Actor profile id
actor_profile_id.description: A stable, opaque id for the actor's Workspace profile (actor.profileId); survives an email rename.

actor_caller_type.label: Actor caller type
actor_caller_type.description: What kind of entity performed the action (actor.callerType), for example USER.

source_ip.label: Source IP address
source_ip.description: The address the request behind this activity came from (ipAddress).

application_name.label: Application name
application_name.description: Which Reports API application the item belongs to (id.applicationName); one of a fixed set of values the activities.list reference names.

customer_id.label: Customer id
customer_id.description: The Workspace customer the item belongs to (id.customerId).

unique_qualifier.label: Unique qualifier
unique_qualifier.description: The item's own id (id.uniqueQualifier), unique only when paired with id.time and id.applicationName.

owner_domain.label: Owner domain
owner_domain.description: The primary domain of the Workspace account the item belongs to, when the API sets it (ownerDomain).

event_type.label: Event type
event_type.description: The category an item's event falls into within its application (events[].type).

event_name.label: Event name
event_name.description: The specific event within its type (events[].name); each application's own appendix page names its own event catalog, not reproduced here.

event_parameters.label: Event parameters
event_parameters.description: The event's own name/value detail, an array of {name, value|boolValue|intValue|multiValue} (events[].parameters).

etag.label: Etag
etag.description: The item's own etag, as the Reports API returns it (etag).

kind.label: Resource kind
kind.description: A fixed resource-type string the API sets on every item, admin#reports#activity (kind).

asset_id.label: Asset id
asset_id.description: The Data Studio asset's own id (object_id, asset_id).

asset_type.label: Asset type
asset_type.description: What kind of Data Studio asset this is, for example DATA_SOURCE (object_category, asset_type).

owner_principal.label: Owner
owner_principal.description: The asset's owner, by email; the TA writes the same value onto four aliases (owner, owner_email, owner_id, owner_mail) so none of the four is a stable numeric id despite the _id name.

visibility.label: Visibility
visibility.description: Who can access the asset, for example PRIVATE (visibility).

asset_extra_attrs.label: Extra attributes
asset_extra_attrs.description: Event parameters the TA has no field of their own for, joined as KEY:VALUE (object_attrs).

product_label.label: Product label
product_label.description: A fixed product name the TA writes onto every event, Google Data Studio (dvc, vendor_product).

change_action.label: Change action
change_action.description: The change's own verb, in two forms the TA writes side by side: the raw event name (signature) and a lower-case, past-tense normalisation (action).

counterpart_principal.label: Counterpart principal
counterpart_principal.description: A second identity a change names besides the actor, when the change involves one (src_user, src_user_name, src_user_type).
counterpart_principal.notes: Null on the one captured CREATE event; src_user, src_user_name and src_user_type are present in the observed schema. Google's own appendix documents a TARGET_USER_EMAIL parameter and a CHANGE_USER_ACCESS event naming a second identity a sharing change involves, which is what these columns are expected to carry when populated.

parent_asset.label: Parent asset
parent_asset.description: The id of a containing asset, when the changed asset is nested (parent_object, parent_object_category, parent_object_id).
parent_asset.notes: Null on the one captured CREATE event; parent_object, parent_object_category and parent_object_id are present in the observed schema. parent_object is not a Splunk Change data model field; Google's own appendix documents a PARENT_WORKSPACE_ID parameter and a PARENT_WORKSPACE_CHANGE event, which is what these columns are expected to carry when populated.

change_outcome.label: Change outcome
change_outcome.description: Outcome and change-kind detail the Change data model reserves fields for (change_type, command, result, result_id, status).
change_outcome.notes: Populated as null on the one captured CREATE event. change_type, command, result, result_id and status are documented fields of Splunk's own Change data model (All_Changes dataset); the TA writes the same field names, present in the observed schema, empty on this event.

ip_shared.text: A NAT gateway, VPN exit or shared proxy can put many people behind one address; a match is a lead, not a link.

names_not_stable.text: An actor or owner is identified by email; a rename or alias change moves the identifier, not the person.

time_basis.text: id.time is when Google recorded the activity; Splunk's index time, set on ingest, can lag well behind it.

qualifier_scope.text: id.uniqueQualifier repeats across applications and across days; it is only unique paired with id.time and id.applicationName.

id_name_is_not_an_id.text: user_id, owner_id, owner_mail and user_name carry the actor's email, not a stable id, on the captured event; actor.profileId is the real stable id, and asset_id/object_id/parent_object_id are GUIDs naming a different thing again.
